"AQUARIA: FISHING WORLDS ONLINE

A 2D Multiplayer Fishing Sandbox MMORPG

PROJECT TYPE: 2D Side-View Pixel-Art Sandbox MMORPG
PLATFORM: Android Mobile + Desktop Web
ART DIRECTION: Modern Detailed Pixel Art (16-bit / 32-bit inspired)
TARGET PERFORMANCE: 60 FPS
MULTIPLAYER TARGET: 10–15 real players per world/room
MAIN GAMEPLAY: Fishing, Exploration, Habitat Building, Crafting and Social Multiplayer.

1. GAME VISION

Create an original, beautiful and fully playable 2D fishing sandbox MMORPG named AQUARIA.

AQUARIA is a living online world where players can fish, explore, collect rare fish, build their own environments, create custom aquatic habitats, craft equipment, trade with other players and develop their own fishing identity.

Fishing must be the main activity, but players must also have complete freedom to build and customize their own worlds.

The game must feel like a real persistent sandbox MMORPG, not a simple fishing simulator or a static prototype.

IMPORTANT:
Use the attached concept art as visual direction. Do not reproduce the poster as a single game screen. Build the actual game, separate game assets, UI, environments and gameplay systems.

Create original characters, environments, creatures, item designs and world structures.

2. WORLD AND CHARACTER DESIGN

Create a 2D side-view tile-based world.

Character features:

- Customizable character appearance.
- Multiple hairstyles.
- Different outfits.
- Hats and accessories.
- Fishing animations.
- Walking and running animations.
- Jumping and falling animations.
- Idle animations.
- Rod casting and reeling animations.
- Different fishing poses.

Movement:

- Walk left and right.
- Jump.
- Climb ladders.
- Stand on platforms.
- Interact with objects.
- Enter different environments.

World features:

- Forests.
- Lakes.
- Rivers.
- Waterfalls.
- Beaches.
- Oceans.
- Caves.
- Mountains.
- Snow environments.
- Tropical islands.
- Hidden fishing locations.

Create a seamless and expandable tile-based world.

3. BUILDING AND BLOCK SYSTEM

Players must be able to construct their own worlds.

Implement:

- Grid-based block placement.
- Block removal.
- Block inventory.
- Block stacking.
- Building mode.
- World saving.
- Personal building areas.

Block categories:

NATURAL BLOCKS:
Grass, dirt, stone, sand, mud, snow, ice, clay and crystal.

BUILDING BLOCKS:
Wood, stone bricks, glass, metal, decorative tiles and platforms.

AQUATIC BLOCKS:
Water blocks, deep-water blocks, freshwater blocks and special biome water blocks.

DECORATIVE BLOCKS:
Corals, aquatic plants, glowing crystals, seaweed, flowers, lanterns and underwater decorations.

INTERACTIVE OBJECTS:
Doors, chests, signs, ladders, workbenches, fishing stations, aquarium tanks and display stands.

Water blocks are extremely important.

Players must be able to place water blocks to construct their own ponds, lakes, rivers, swimming pools and fishing environments.

The water system should support different depths and visual appearances.

4. ADVANCED FISHING MECHANICS

Fishing is the core gameplay system.

Implement a complete fishing process:

1. Equip a fishing rod.
2. Select bait or lure.
3. Stand near suitable water.
4. Cast the fishing line.
5. Wait for a fish to bite.
6. Display a visual bite indicator.
7. Start a fishing timing minigame.
8. Control tension while reeling.
9. Successfully catch the fish.
10. Display fish name, rarity, weight and value.
11. Automatically add the fish to inventory.

Fishing must be interactive.

Include:

- Casting distance.
- Reel speed.
- Fishing tension.
- Line durability.
- Fish resistance.
- Fish escape probability.
- Bite timing.
- Different fish behaviours.

Large fish should be harder to catch.

Rare fish should require better equipment, suitable bait or special environmental conditions.

5. FISHING RODS

Create a large fishing rod progression system.

Rod types:

1. Beginner Rod.
2. Wooden Rod.
3. Fiberglass Rod.
4. Carbon Rod.
5. Professional Rod.
6. Deep Sea Rod.
7. Golden Rod.
8. Crystal Rod.
9. Ancient Rod.
10. Legendary Rod.
11. Mythical Rod.

Every rod must have its own appearance and statistics.

Rod statistics:

- Casting Distance.
- Reel Speed.
- Line Strength.
- Fish Control.
- Luck.
- Rarity Bonus.
- Durability.

Some rods should specialize in certain fishing environments.

Examples:

- Deep Sea Rod: better deep-water performance.
- Crystal Rod: special bonuses in crystal habitats.
- Golden Rod: improved general fishing statistics.
- Ancient Rod: special bonuses against ancient fish.

Create unique visual effects for rare and high-tier rods.

6. REELS, LINES AND HOOKS

Fishing equipment must be customizable.

Reel categories:

- Basic Reel.
- Bronze Reel.
- Steel Reel.
- Advanced Reel.
- Precision Reel.
- Deep Sea Reel.
- Legendary Reel.

Fishing line categories:

- Basic Line.
- Nylon Line.
- Fluorocarbon Line.
- Braided Line.
- Reinforced Line.
- Deep Sea Line.
- Mythical Line.

Hook categories:

- Small Hook.
- Medium Hook.
- Large Hook.
- Barbed Hook.
- Heavy Hook.
- Special Hook.

Different equipment must affect fish-catching performance.

For example, a stronger line should help catch heavy fish, while a precision reel should improve tension control.

7. LURES AND BAIT

Create a detailed bait and lure collection.

LURES:

- Spinner.
- Spoon.
- Minnow.
- Frog.
- Crankbait.
- Soft Plastic.
- Glow Lure.
- Crystal Lure.
- Deep Sea Lure.
- Electric Lure.
- Legendary Lure.
- Mythical Lure.

NATURAL BAIT:

- Worms.
- Grubs.
- Insects.
- Small Minnows.
- Shrimp.
- Crustaceans.
- Special Bait.

Different species must prefer different bait and lures.

Examples:

- Worms attract common freshwater fish.
- Minnows attract predatory fish.
- Glow Lures work better at night.
- Shrimp attracts certain tropical and coastal fish.
- Deep Sea Lures attract ocean species.
- Special Lures unlock rare fishing opportunities.

Lures should have different effectiveness, durability and rarity.

8. ACCESSORIES AND BUFF SYSTEM

Create a comprehensive equipment and accessory system.

Equipment slots:

- Headgear.
- Necklace.
- Gloves.
- Ring.
- Boots.
- Backpack.
- Special Charm.

Examples:

Lucky Necklace:
Increases rare fish probability.

Angler Hat:
Increases fishing experience.

Precision Gloves:
Improves fishing control.

Golden Ring:
Provides additional luck.

Deep Sea Charm:
Improves deep-water fishing.

Treasure Compass:
Increases treasure discovery chances.

Explorer Boots:
Improves movement speed.

Fishing Backpack:
Increases inventory capacity.

Crystal Pendant:
Improves fishing in crystal habitats.

Accessories must have different rarity levels:

Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythical.

Allow players to combine equipment bonuses.

Prevent unlimited stacking and maintain balanced gameplay.

9. FISH COLLECTION AND RARITY

Create a large and expandable fish database.

Rarity categories:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.
- Mythical.
- Secret.

Every fish must have:

- Unique sprite.
- Name.
- Description.
- Rarity.
- Weight range.
- Selling price.
- Preferred biome.
- Preferred depth.
- Preferred bait.
- Preferred time.
- Catch probability.

EXAMPLE FISH COLLECTION:

COMMON:
Bluegill, River Minnow, Small Carp, Catfish, Silver Perch.

UNCOMMON:
Rainbow Trout, Red Snapper, Yellowfin, Mudfish.

RARE:
Golden Koi, Electric Eel, Crystal Perch, Emerald Pike.

EPIC:
Shadow Bass, Frostfin, Phantom Ray, Thunder Eel.

LEGENDARY:
Ancient Dragonfish, Golden Leviathan, Phantom Marlin.

MYTHICAL:
Celestial Whale, Abyssal Serpent, Eternal Koi.

SECRET:
Create hidden fish species with extremely rare discovery conditions.

Fish must have randomized weights within their species-specific weight ranges.

A 2 kg fish and a 20 kg fish of the same species should not necessarily have the same selling price.

Add personal records and fish collection achievements.

10. CUSTOM AQUATIC HABITATS

THIS IS ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT FEATURES OF AQUARIA.

Players must be able to create their own fishing habitats using water blocks and environmental blocks.

Build a habitat recognition system that detects:

- Water volume.
- Water depth.
- Block composition.
- Nearby vegetation.
- Special decorations.
- Environmental conditions.

BIOME EXAMPLES:

FRESHWATER POND:
Water + Dirt + Grass.

TROPICAL HABITAT:
Water + Sand + Coral + Tropical Plants.

DEEP OCEAN:
Large water volume + sufficient depth.

FROZEN LAKE:
Water + Ice + Snow.

SWAMP:
Water + Mud + Swamp Vegetation.

CRYSTAL HABITAT:
Water + Crystal Blocks + Glowing Decorations.

VOLCANIC HABITAT:
Water + Volcanic Rocks + Special Decorations.

MAGICAL HABITAT:
Water + Rare Crystals + Special Biome Objects.

Players must be able to build these habitats in different shapes and sizes.

Do not limit players to predefined lakes or rivers.

FISH SPAWNING RULES:

- Tropical fish require tropical habitats.
- Deep sea fish require sufficient depth.
- Frozen fish prefer frozen environments.
- Swamp fish prefer muddy environments.
- Crystal fish require special environmental conditions.
- Secret fish require special block combinations or discovery conditions.

Create a Habitat Information Panel displaying:

- Habitat Type.
- Water Depth.
- Habitat Quality.
- Fish Species Available.
- Environmental Requirements.
- Rare Fish Conditions.

Allow players to discover new habitat combinations.

11. UNDERWATER ENVIRONMENT

Create beautiful underwater visual environments.

Features:

- Animated water.
- Underwater lighting.
- Bubbles.
- Aquatic plants.
- Coral reefs.
- Rocks.
- Underwater caves.
- Swimming fish.
- Rare underwater treasures.

Fish should move naturally within suitable water areas.

Different fish should have different movement patterns and swimming speeds.

12. CRAFTING AND ECONOMY

Implement a functional crafting system.

Crafting stations:

- Workbench.
- Fishing Equipment Table.
- Bait Station.
- Reel Workshop.
- Aquarium.
- Fish Display Station.

Players can craft:

- Fishing rods.
- Reels.
- Fishing lines.
- Hooks.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Accessories.
- Building blocks.
- Decorative objects.

Economy:

- Sell fish.
- Buy equipment.
- Trade items.
- Purchase bait.
- Upgrade equipment.
- Earn coins through quests.
- Open player shops.

Create a balanced in-game currency system.

13. MULTIPLAYER MMORPG

REAL MULTIPLAYER IS A CORE REQUIREMENT.

Target 10–15 real players per shared world or room.

Features:

- Player accounts.
- Unique usernames.
- Real-time player movement.
- Player appearance synchronization.
- Shared environments.
- Player chat.
- Friends system.
- Private messages if supported.
- Fishing together.
- Trading.
- Player shops.
- Visiting player habitats.
- Fishing competitions.
- Leaderboards.

Players must be able to see each other moving, jumping and fishing in real time.

Do not simulate multiplayer using NPCs or duplicated local characters.

Use a real networking backend and server-authoritative state if supported.

Save player data and world changes persistently.

If the platform cannot support real multiplayer directly, explain the exact missing backend or networking requirements and build the game with a multiplayer-ready architecture.

Do not falsely claim that multiplayer is functional if it is only simulated.

14. PROGRESSION AND SKILLS

Create a player leveling system.

Player progression categories:

- Fishing Level.
- Building Level.
- Exploration Level.
- Crafting Level.

Players gain experience through:

- Catching fish.
- Discovering new species.
- Completing fishing challenges.
- Exploring new biomes.
- Building habitats.
- Crafting equipment.

Higher levels unlock:

- Better fishing rods.
- New lures.
- Special accessories.
- New fish species.
- New crafting recipes.
- New environments.
- Advanced building blocks.

Create achievements and milestones.

15. INVENTORY AND FISH JOURNAL

Build a fully functional inventory.

Inventory categories:

- Fish.
- Rods.
- Reels.
- Lines.
- Hooks.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Accessories.
- Blocks.
- Materials.
- Consumables.
- Quest Items.

Features:

- Item stacking.
- Item sorting.
- Item descriptions.
- Equipment slots.
- Rarity indicators.
- Item statistics.
- Sell and trade functions.

FISH JOURNAL:

Create a fish collection book.

Show:

- Discovered species.
- Undiscovered fish silhouettes.
- Fish descriptions.
- Rarity.
- Weight records.
- Preferred habitat.
- Preferred bait.
- Personal catch records.

16. QUESTS AND EVENTS

Add fishing quests and exploration missions.

Examples:

- Catch 10 common fish.
- Catch a fish above 10 kg.
- Discover a new biome.
- Build a tropical habitat.
- Catch a legendary fish.
- Help another player.
- Find a secret fish.

Add limited-time fishing competitions and seasonal events.

17. DAY/NIGHT AND WEATHER SYSTEM

Create:

- Sunrise.
- Daytime.
- Sunset.
- Nighttime.
- Rain.
- Fog.
- Snow.
- Storms.

Fish availability should change depending on time and weather.

Some fish only appear:

- During nighttime.
- During rain.
- At sunrise.
- During storms.
- Under special environmental conditions.

18. PETS AND COSMETICS

Allow players to collect cosmetic pets and companions.

Examples:

- Small Turtle.
- Blue Fish Companion.
- Floating Jellyfish.
- Baby Dragonfish.
- Crystal Crab.

Pets may provide small cosmetic or utility bonuses, but must not overpower fishing equipment.

Add outfits, hairstyles, fishing animations and character customization.

19. USER INTERFACE AND CONTROLS

Create a polished, responsive mobile-friendly UI.

Main interface:

- Player Profile.
- Health or character status if needed.
- Currency.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Fish Journal.
- Crafting.
- Habitat Information.
- Map.
- Quests.
- Shop.
- Friends.
- Chat.
- Settings.

MOBILE CONTROLS:

- Virtual movement joystick.
- Jump button.
- Interact button.
- Cast Fishing button.
- Reel button.
- Inventory button.
- Building Mode button.

DESKTOP CONTROLS:

- Keyboard movement.
- Jump controls.
- Mouse interaction.
- Keyboard shortcuts.

Make all UI elements functional.

Avoid controls covering the main gameplay area.

20. VISUAL ART DIRECTION

Use the attached AQUARIA concept artwork as the main visual reference.

Create an original modern detailed pixel-art aesthetic.

Visual requirements:

- Medium-sized detailed pixel art.
- 16-bit/32-bit-inspired style.
- Smooth character animations.
- Beautiful turquoise and deep blue water.
- Detailed vegetation.
- Rich natural environments.
- Unique fish silhouettes.
- Beautiful equipment sprites.
- Distinctive biome designs.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Attractive underwater effects.

Do not use excessively tiny pixels.

Do not create blurry or low-resolution-looking assets.

Do not copy existing game characters, logos, maps, UI or proprietary assets.

Maintain visual consistency across all environments and items.

21. PERFORMANCE AND TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

Target 60 FPS.

Optimize for Android mobile devices and desktop browsers.

Requirements:

- Efficient tile rendering.
- Optimized character movement.
- Lightweight animations.
- Responsive UI.
- Efficient multiplayer synchronization.
- Persistent data storage.
- Modular architecture.
- Reusable game components.

Keep game data organized in structured JSON or equivalent data definitions where possible.

Separate:

- Fish database.
- Rod database.
- Lure database.
- Accessory database.
- Block database.
- Biome rules.
- Crafting recipes.
- Player statistics.

Make it easy to add new fish, equipment, habitats and content without rebuilding the entire game.

22. ADMIN AND DEBUG SYSTEM

If supported, create an administrator system.

Authorized administrators can:

- Spawn fish.
- Add items.
- Adjust rarity.
- Modify fish weights.
- Modify fishing probabilities.
- Edit equipment statistics.
- Create new species.
- Inspect player information.
- Manage world data.

Protect administrator access with proper authorization.

23. DEVELOPMENT ORDER

Do not attempt to generate every feature simultaneously if doing so reduces quality.

Build the game in stages.

STAGE 1 — CORE PLAYABLE GAME:

- Character movement.
- World generation.
- Tile-based building.
- Water blocks.
- Basic fishing.
- 10 initial fish species.
- Basic fishing rods.
- Inventory.
- Saving and loading.

STAGE 2 — ADVANCED FISHING:

- Multiple rods.
- Reels.
- Lines.
- Hooks.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Accessories.
- Buffs.
- Fish rarity.
- Fish weight.
- Fishing Journal.

STAGE 3 — HABITAT SYSTEM:

- Custom water environments.
- Biome detection.
- Water depth.
- Habitat quality.
- Fish spawning rules.
- Secret fish conditions.

STAGE 4 — MULTIPLAYER:

- Player accounts.
- Real-time movement.
- Shared worlds.
- Chat.
- Trading.
- Friends.
- Persistent multiplayer data.
- 10–15 player target.

STAGE 5 — EXPANSION:

- More fish.
- More biomes.
- More blocks.
- Advanced crafting.
- Quests.
- Events.
- Pets.
- Leaderboards.
- Special discoveries.

24. FIRST BUILD INSTRUCTIONS

START BUILDING NOW.

Do not simply explain how the game could be created.

Generate the actual playable Stage 1 game.

Prioritize:

1. A beautiful playable 2D pixel-art environment.
2. Functional player movement.
3. Functional water block placement and removal.
4. Functional fishing mechanics.
5. Functional fish catching.
6. Inventory and fish collection.
7. Persistent player progress.

After the first build, test all important interactions.

Do not create decorative buttons that do nothing.

If a feature is not supported, explain the limitation and continue implementing the working features.

FINAL VISION

AQUARIA must become a living, expandable online fishing sandbox MMORPG.

Every player should be able to develop their own fishing style, build unique aquatic habitats, discover rare fish, collect powerful equipment, explore beautiful environments and interact with other players.

The world should encourage creativity, exploration, competition and social interaction.

FISH MORE. BUILD BETTER. EXPLORE DEEPER. BECOME A LEGEND.

WELCOME TO AQUARIA — FISHING WORLDS ONLINE.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Stage 1 of “AQUARIA: FISHING WORLDS ONLINE,” a 2D side-view pixel-art fishing sandbox MMORPG.
- Deliver a polished browser game with movement, fishing, building, inventory, saving, and clear multiplayer limitations.

## Requirements
- Create original modern detailed pixel-art presentation and a separate game environment/UI, not a poster.
- Implement Stage 1 gameplay: character movement, tile world, water placement/removal, fishing, 10 fish species, basic rods, inventory, and persistent progress.
- Make all controls functional; do not add decorative nonfunctional buttons.
- Keep the game mobile-friendly and suitable for desktop.
- Real multiplayer should not be falsely represented as implemented.

## Decisions
- Implemented the first build as a single-player, local-save browser game.
- Used original canvas-rendered pixel-art visuals and a persistent local storage save system.
- Marked multiplayer as requiring an account service, authoritative game server, and persistent multiplayer database.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the complete main game shell and responsive UI.
- Added animated pixel-art cove environment, player character, camera, terrain, water, reeds, plants, clouds, and lighting.
- Added left/right movement, jumping, canvas interaction, touch controls, and keyboard controls.
- Added building mode, block selection, block placement/removal, and block inventory.
- Added custom water blocks and persistent world edits.
- Added casting, bite timing, tension/reeling minigame, randomized weighted catches, rarity, coins, and fish capture modal.
- Added 10 initial fish species in the fish database logic.
- Added inventory, selling fish, fish journal, habitat scanner, map, quests, crafting, and settings panels.
- Added automatic local saving for coins, catches, records, inventory, blocks, world edits, and player position.
- Added a local HTTP server on port 3002 for browser testing.

### Active
- No active implementation work remains in this conversation.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer is unavailable in the current architecture and is explicitly documented as a backend-dependent feature.
- No real player accounts, shared rooms, chat, trading, friends, leaderboards, or server-authoritative persistence were implemented.

## Next Move
1. Add the missing real multiplayer backend and account system if Stage 4 is to be implemented.
2. Browser-test and refine fishing, building, and mobile touch interactions.
3. Expand beyond Stage 1 with additional rods, reels, lines, hooks, bait, habitats, quests, and pet/cosmetic systems.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/index.html`: Main game markup and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/style.css`: Full visual styling and responsive/mobile layout.
- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/game.js`: Game logic, rendering, saving, fishing, building, and modal systems.

## Important Context
- Stage 1 is implemented as a locally persistent browser game; there are no simulated multiplayer players.
- Progress is stored in browser `localStorage` under key `aquaria-stage1-v1`.
- The game can be served locally with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Untracked/changed project files include `index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js`, `README.md`, `Agents.md`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, `capture.sh`, and existing environment files.

"AQUARIA — MAJOR GAMEPLAY CONTROL & INVENTORY UPDATE V1.1

IMPORTANT:
Update the EXISTING AQUARIA project. Do not create a new project, delete the existing world, redesign the entire game, or replace working systems.

Preserve the current visual style, character, world, terrain, water, environment, existing progress and working features.

This update focuses on:

1. Character movement and collision fixes.
2. Anti-stuck and unstuck systems.
3. Fully functional mobile controls.
4. Customizable HUD editor.
5. Eight-slot inventory hotbar.
6. Item dropping and pickup.
7. Fist and Wrench tool modes.
8. World block and object interaction.
9. Functional vending machines.
10. Settings and control customization.

All new features must be functional, not decorative.

1. FIX CHARACTER MOVEMENT AND COLLISION

The current character appears stationary and may be trapped inside or against terrain blocks.

Investigate and fix the actual movement and collision logic.

Implement a proper 2D character controller.

MOVEMENT:

- Move left.
- Move right.
- Jump.
- Fall naturally.
- Land on solid platforms.
- Walk across terrain.
- Stop when blocked by solid walls.
- Move smoothly across different terrain heights.
- Interact with nearby objects.
- Support swimming when inside water.

Use reliable axis-based collision detection.

The character must not:

- Spawn inside solid blocks.
- Get stuck inside terrain.
- Pass through solid blocks unintentionally.
- Become permanently frozen.
- Get trapped between two collision surfaces.
- Fall through the ground.
- Teleport unexpectedly.

Implement proper gravity, collision resolution and grounded detection.

The character must have separate states:

- Idle.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Jumping.
- Falling.
- Swimming.
- Fishing.
- Interacting.
- Using tools.

Animations must reflect the actual movement state.

2. MOBILE MOVEMENT CONTROLS

Create fully functional mobile touch controls.

LEFT SIDE:

- Left movement button.
- Right movement button.

RIGHT SIDE:

- Jump button.
- Action button.
- Tool button.

Movement buttons must support continuous movement while being held down.

Jump should trigger only when appropriate.

Implement:

- Touch press.
- Touch hold.
- Touch release.
- Responsive input handling.
- Input priority.
- No accidental repeated jumps.
- No stuck movement when a finger leaves the screen.

Allow simultaneous movement and jumping.

The character should move continuously while the directional button is held.

IMPORTANT:
Do not make movement buttons respond only to a single tap. Holding the movement button must continuously move the character.

3. ANTI-STUCK AND UNSTUCK SYSTEM

Create a reliable anti-stuck system.

Add an UNSTUCK option in Settings.

When the player becomes trapped:

- Detect invalid character positions.
- Detect collision overlap with solid blocks.
- Detect movement failure.
- Search for the nearest safe position.
- Move the character to the nearest valid empty position.

Add a manual UNSTUCK button.

When pressed:

1. Check the current character position.
2. Search nearby safe positions.
3. Find a valid position outside solid blocks.
4. Move the character safely.
5. Restore normal movement and collision.

If no nearby safe position exists, teleport the player to the latest safe spawn point.

Add a Respawn option as a separate function.

Do not reset inventory, currency, equipment or world progress when using Unstuck.

Also add:

- Save last safe position.
- Safe spawn protection.
- Recovery from falling outside the playable world.
- Recovery from invalid terrain collisions.

Unstuck must never delete the player's items or world structures.

4. EIGHT-SLOT QUICK ACCESS HOTBAR

THIS IS A MAJOR FEATURE.

Create a permanent eight-slot quick access item bar at the bottom of the gameplay screen.

The hotbar must be inspired by classic sandbox MMORPG inventory systems, but use original AQUARIA artwork and interface design.

Create exactly 8 visible item slots.

Each slot must support:

- An item icon.
- Item quantity.
- Item rarity border.
- Selected item highlight.
- Empty slot appearance.
- Cooldown indicator if necessary.

SLOT BEHAVIOUR:

Slot 1 to Slot 8 can contain:

- Fishing rods.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Building blocks.
- Tools.
- Consumables.
- Special items.

Players must be able to:

- Select an item by tapping its slot.
- Switch between items instantly.
- Drag items between slots.
- Move inventory items into the hotbar.
- Remove items from hotbar slots.
- Rearrange the hotbar.
- Use the selected item.

On desktop, support keyboard number keys 1–8.

On mobile, tapping a slot must select that item.

The currently selected slot must be visually highlighted.

The selected item must become the active usable item.

If a fishing rod is selected, the character should hold the rod.

If a building block is selected, the character enters block placement mode.

If bait is selected, allow it to be equipped or used according to its item type.

If a consumable is selected, allow the player to activate it.

Empty slots must not activate anything.

The hotbar must remain visible during normal gameplay and must not cover important character or world areas.

5. INVENTORY AND ITEM MANAGEMENT

Create a fully functional inventory system.

Each item must have:

- Unique item ID.
- Name.
- Icon.
- Description.
- Item category.
- Rarity.
- Quantity.
- Maximum stack size.
- Usage type.
- Tradeable status.
- Drop status.

Inventory categories:

- Fishing Equipment.
- Rods.
- Reels.
- Lines.
- Hooks.
- Lures.
- Bait.
- Accessories.
- Building Blocks.
- Tools.
- Consumables.
- Special Items.

Implement:

- Item selection.
- Item movement.
- Item sorting.
- Item dropping.
- Item pickup.
- Item usage.
- Item selling.
- Item storage.

Inventory changes must update the hotbar automatically.

If an item is dropped or consumed, update the corresponding hotbar slot immediately.

6. DROP AND PICKUP SYSTEM

Every eligible physical item must be droppable into the world.

When dropping an item:

- Create a visible item sprite.
- Place it near the character.
- Apply a small drop animation.
- Display its icon.
- Allow the player to pick it up again.

When a player approaches a dropped item:

- Display an interaction indicator.
- Show the item name.
- Show its quantity.
- Allow pickup using the Action button.

Add an optional automatic pickup setting.

If automatic pickup is enabled, nearby items can be collected automatically.

If disabled, players must press the Action button.

DROPPED ITEM RULES:

- Dropped items must remain visible.
- Items must have collision or ground placement.
- Items must not spawn inside solid blocks.
- Items must disappear after successful pickup.
- Items must be added to inventory correctly.
- Items must not duplicate.
- Multiplayer item ownership and pickup must be synchronized if online multiplayer is supported.

Prevent item duplication through repeated interaction or network requests.

7. FIST AND WRENCH TOOL SYSTEM

Create a dedicated tool mode button.

This button must switch between two modes:

MODE 1 — FIST

Display a fist icon.

The fist is the default interaction tool.

Functions:

- Punch certain breakable objects.
- Interact with basic world objects.
- Activate nearby objects.
- Perform basic hand actions.

MODE 2 — WRENCH

When the player presses the tool button again, switch to Wrench mode.

Display a wrench icon.

Functions:

- Edit nearby blocks.
- Remove eligible blocks.
- Repair eligible objects.
- Modify placed structures.
- Interact with editable world objects.
- Open object editing options.

The selected tool must be clearly displayed.

Pressing the tool button should toggle:

FIST → WRENCH → FIST.

Do not confuse the tool toggle with the selected hotbar item.

The tool mode and hotbar must work together.

8. WORLD INTERACTION AND EDITING

Create a proximity-based world editing system.

When the character is near an editable block or object:

1. Detect nearby objects.
2. Check the direction the character is facing.
3. Highlight the target object.
4. Display an interaction outline.
5. Allow interaction through the Action button.

WRENCH INTERACTION:

If the target is a removable block:

- Remove the block.
- Add the block to inventory when appropriate.
- Update the world visually.

If the target is an editable object:

- Open its editing panel.
- Display available actions.
- Allow the player to modify it.

If the target is a chest:

- Open the chest inventory.

If the target is a vending machine:

- Open the vending machine interface.

If the target is a fishing station:

- Open the fishing station interface.

If the target is a water block:

- Allow eligible water placement and removal operations.

BLOCK PLACEMENT:

When a building block is selected from the hotbar:

- Display a placement preview.
- Snap the block to the world grid.
- Show whether placement is valid.
- Tap or press the Action button to place it.
- Deduct one item from inventory.
- Update the world immediately.

Prevent placing blocks inside the player character or occupied solid spaces.

9. VENDING MACHINE SYSTEM

Create functional vending machines throughout the world.

Vending machines should display:

- Item icon.
- Item name.
- Description.
- Price.
- Item rarity.
- Purchase button.
- Ownership status.

Examples:

- Basic Fishing Rod.
- Worm Bait.
- Small Hooks.
- Fishing Lines.
- Basic Lures.
- Building Blocks.
- Utility Tools.
- Accessories.

IMPORTANT ITEM OWNERSHIP RULE:

For non-stackable equipment and unique vending-machine products, each player can own only ONE copy of each item at a time.

Example:
If a player already owns one Golden Rod, the vending machine must not allow the player to purchase another Golden Rod.

Display:
ALREADY OWNED.

For eligible stackable consumables, allow quantities according to their defined maximum stack size.

The vending machine must:

- Check player currency.
- Check item ownership.
- Check inventory capacity.
- Deduct the correct price.
- Add the purchased item.
- Update the inventory and hotbar.
- Save the transaction.

Prevent double purchases caused by repeated tapping.

The purchase system must never duplicate items or deduct currency without granting the item.

10. CUSTOMIZABLE HUD EDITOR

Create a full HUD customization menu inside Settings.

Call it:

HUD EDITOR.

Players must be able to customize their mobile control layout.

Allow editing of:

- Left movement button.
- Right movement button.
- Jump button.
- Action button.
- Fist/Wrench button.
- Fishing button.
- Inventory button.
- Eight-slot hotbar.
- Other gameplay buttons.

HUD EDITING OPTIONS:

1. Move buttons to different screen positions.
2. Resize buttons.
3. Adjust button opacity.
4. Adjust button spacing.
5. Change button layout.
6. Show or hide eligible interface elements.
7. Reset to default layout.

Support touch-and-drag repositioning.

Provide a visible editing grid.

Display a live preview while editing.

Do not allow essential controls to be permanently hidden.

Save customized HUD settings locally and restore them when the player returns.

Add:

- Default HUD preset.
- Compact HUD preset.
- Large Button preset.
- Custom HUD preset.

The HUD must adapt to different Android screen sizes and aspect ratios.

11. SETTINGS MENU

Expand the existing Settings interface.

Create the following categories:

CONTROLS:

- Movement sensitivity.
- Button layout.
- Button size.
- Button opacity.
- Jump behaviour.
- Auto-run if supported.
- HUD editor.

GAMEPLAY:

- Auto pickup ON/OFF.
- Fishing assistance ON/OFF.
- Interaction range indicator.
- Item drop confirmation.
- Camera follow.
- Unstuck.
- Respawn.

GRAPHICS:

- Graphics quality.
- Animation quality.
- Particle effects.
- Water effects.
- Visual effects.

AUDIO:

- Music volume.
- Sound effects volume.
- Mute option.

ACCESSIBILITY:

- Larger buttons.
- High contrast interface.
- Reduced visual effects.

Save all player settings persistently.

12. CHARACTER CAMERA AND SCREEN POSITION

Improve the camera system.

The camera should follow the character smoothly.

The character should remain visible and properly positioned during movement.

Support:

- Horizontal camera movement.
- Vertical camera adjustment where necessary.
- Camera boundaries.
- Smooth camera transitions.

Prevent the character from disappearing behind HUD elements.

Add an optional camera reset button.

13. ITEM AND INTERACTION FEEDBACK

Add visual feedback to important actions.

Examples:

- Item pickup notification.
- Item dropped notification.
- Item used notification.
- Block placed notification.
- Block removed notification.
- Purchase successful notification.
- Insufficient currency warning.
- Inventory full warning.
- Already owned warning.

Use short, clean animations.

Do not overload the screen with unnecessary notifications.

14. SAVE AND PERSISTENCE

Save:

- Character position.
- Inventory.
- Eight hotbar slots.
- Selected hotbar slot.
- Current tool mode.
- Currency.
- Equipment.
- HUD layout.
- Settings.
- World block changes.

When the player exits and returns, restore the saved state.

Do not reset existing player progress.

Use reliable save operations to avoid item duplication or loss.

15. MULTIPLAYER COMPATIBILITY

Prepare these systems for multiplayer.

If real multiplayer networking is supported:

- Synchronize player movements.
- Synchronize dropped items.
- Synchronize block placement and removal.
- Synchronize item pickups.
- Synchronize trading.
- Synchronize vending transactions.
- Synchronize world changes.

Use server-side validation for important item and currency transactions.

Do not allow two players to pick up the same unique dropped item.

If multiplayer is not currently supported, build the systems modularly so networking can be added later.

16. TESTING AND VALIDATION

After implementing the update, test the following:

MOVEMENT TEST:

- Hold left and right.
- Jump while moving.
- Walk across platforms.
- Enter water.
- Check collision against blocks.

UNSTUCK TEST:

- Intentionally place the character in an invalid or blocked position.
- Activate Unstuck.
- Verify safe recovery.
- Verify inventory remains intact.

HOTBAR TEST:

- Put different items into all 8 slots.
- Select each slot.
- Switch items.
- Use items.
- Verify selected item highlighting.

DROP/PICKUP TEST:

- Drop an item.
- Confirm it appears in the world.
- Pick it up again.
- Confirm inventory quantity updates correctly.

TOOL TEST:

- Switch Fist to Wrench.
- Switch Wrench to Fist.
- Test block editing.
- Test nearby object interaction.

VENDING TEST:

- Purchase an item.
- Verify currency deduction.
- Verify item ownership.
- Attempt to purchase the same unique item again.
- Confirm duplicate purchase is blocked.

HUD TEST:

- Move buttons.
- Resize buttons.
- Change opacity.
- Save the layout.
- Reload the game.
- Confirm the custom layout remains.

FINAL INSTRUCTION

Implement this update directly in the existing AQUARIA project.

Preserve the current world and existing working features.

Prioritize functional gameplay over decorative interface elements.

Do not create buttons that do nothing.

Do not simulate functionality with fake animations.

All movement, interactions, inventory operations, hotbar selections, item drops, pickups, vending purchases and settings must be connected to actual gameplay logic.

If any feature is unsupported by the current environment, explain the limitation clearly and implement the remaining supported features.

Deliver a fully playable, mobile-friendly control and inventory update."

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Stage 1 of “AQUARIA: FISHING WORLDS ONLINE,” a polished 2D pixel-art fishing sandbox game.
- Browser-test and refine gameplay while clearly distinguishing the local single-player preview from real multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Original detailed pixel-art presentation and functional gameplay/UI on desktop and mobile.
- Implement movement, world building, fishing with 10 species, inventory, and persistent progress.
- Do not portray multiplayer as implemented without real backend support.

## Decisions
- Stage 1 is a single-player browser game with local saves under `aquaria-stage1-v1`.
- Real multiplayer requires accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage; it is not simulated.

## Work State

- Implemented responsive game shell, canvas world, movement, fishing/catch minigame, building, inventory, journal, map, quests, crafting, settings, and local saves.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes.
- Reviewed the key game files and confirmed the existing changes are untracked.

- (none)

- Real multiplayer is not implemented; backend infrastructure is required.

## Next Move
1. Browser-test and refine fishing, building, and mobile interactions.
2. Add real multiplayer backend and account services if Stage 4 is pursued.
3. Expand gameplay with additional equipment, habitats, quests, and cosmetics.

- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/style.css`: Visual styling and responsive layout.

- `/home/runner/work/AQUARIA/AQUARIA/README.md`: Project README.

## Important Context
- The game can be served locally with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `game.js` syntax check passed; no browser test was performed in the latest exchange.
- Project changes are untracked, including `index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js`, `README.md`, `Agents.md`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `capture.sh`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update the existing AQUARIA game with functional movement, mobile controls, hotbar/inventory, item interactions, tools, vending, HUD customization, settings, and persistence while preserving the existing world and features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the current visual style, world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Features should be gameplay-connected, persistent, and mobile-friendly; be honest about multiplayer being unsupported without a real backend.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview; real multiplayer requires backend infrastructure and is not simulated.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial hotbar and pickup-prompt markup, a shop entry point, and expanded touch-control markup in `index.html`.
- Added item metadata and initialized saved-state fields for hotbar, tools, drops, settings, and HUD in `game.js`.
- Improved movement collision sampling, water detection, safe-position recovery, and respawn logic in `game.js`.

### Active
- Wire and implement persistence, hotbar selection/use, tool/action controls, drops/pickups, vending, settings, and HUD controls.
- Add responsive styling for the hotbar and expanded mobile controls.
- Validate movement, interactions, and save restoration.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer remains unsupported without accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage.

## Next Move
1. Update `game.js` persistence and implement hotbar, tool/action controls, item drops/pickups, shop, and settings/HUD interactions.
2. Update `style.css` for the hotbar, pickup prompt, and mobile controls.
3. Run syntax checks and browser-test core gameplay and save restoration.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, physics, state, and interactions; partially updated.
- `index.html`: Game UI, hotbar/shop entry point, and mobile-control markup.
- `style.css`: Existing visual styling and responsive layout; new feature styling remains.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `save()` still persists only the earlier subset of state; new hotbar, settings, HUD, tool, bait, and dropped-item fields are not yet saved.
- `mobileAction`, `mobileTool`, and `shopBtn` are present in markup but not wired.
- Existing controls include `mobileJump`, `mobileCast`, and `mobileReel`; movement buttons use pointer capture.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest edits; no validation has been run since.

## Objective
- Complete gameplay systems in the existing AQUARIA game while preserving its current world, visual style, and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Make features gameplay-connected, persistent, and mobile-friendly; be clear that multiplayer is unsupported without a real backend.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview; real multiplayer requires backend infrastructure and is not simulated.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added hotbar and pickup-prompt markup, a shop entry point, and expanded touch-control markup in `index.html`.
- Added item metadata and initialized state fields for hotbar, tools, dropped items, settings, and HUD in `game.js`.
- Improved movement collision sampling, water detection, safe-position recovery, and respawn logic.
- Updated save serialization to include bait, hotbar, tool mode, dropped items, settings, HUD, selection, and facing.
- Added hotbar rendering/selection, item drop and pickup helpers, settings application, and keyboard shortcuts for slots, dropping, and tool toggling.

### Active
- Finish and wire shop, settings/HUD controls, mobile action/tool controls, and item interactions.
- Add responsive styling for the hotbar, pickup prompt, and mobile controls.
- Validate syntax, gameplay, and save restoration; no validation has been run since the latest edits.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer is unsupported without accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and complete `game.js` interaction wiring; `shopBtn`, `mobileAction`, and `mobileTool` are present but not wired, and the settings modal does not yet expose the initialized settings.
2. Implement or correct bait use, dropped-item rendering/limits, shop purchases, and HUD customization as needed.
3. Add styling in `style.css`, then run `node --check game.js` and browser-test core gameplay and save restoration.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, persistence, movement, fishing, and partially implemented interactions.
- `index.html`: Game UI, hotbar/shop entry point, and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Existing styling; feature-specific styling remains.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `save()` now persists the added state, but newer interaction code and keyboard changes have not been validated.
- `mobileAction`, `mobileTool`, and `shopBtn` are still unwired; settings/HUD controls remain unfinished.
- Existing touch controls include `mobileJump`, `mobileCast`, and `mobileReel`; movement buttons use pointer capture.

- The game remains a single-player local preview; real multiplayer requires backend infrastructure and is not simulated.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete gameplay systems in the existing AQUARIA game while preserving its world, visual style, and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Make features gameplay-connected, persistent, and mobile-friendly; clarify that multiplayer is unsupported without a real backend.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview; real multiplayer requires backend infrastructure and is not simulated.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added hotbar, pickup prompt, shop entry point, and expanded touch-control markup in `index.html`.
- Added item metadata and persistent state for hotbar, tools, dropped items, settings, and HUD in `game.js`.
- Improved movement collision sampling, water detection, safe-position recovery, and respawn logic.
- Expanded save serialization and added hotbar rendering/selection, item drop/pickup helpers, settings application, and keyboard shortcuts.
- Fishing consumes one worm bait per cast, with no-bait feedback and HUD/save updates.
- Wired mobile action/tool handlers, shop-button click handler, and periodic pickup-prompt updates.
- Added persistent controls for auto-pickup, accessibility, HUD visibility, and button opacity.
- Updated crafting so bait and blocks are added to inventory; crafting refreshes HUD and modal.
- Limited dropped items to 24, refreshed pickup prompts after dropping, and added dropped-item world rendering.

### Active
- Define `openShop()` and implement purchases with fund/item validation and persistent state.
- Add responsive styling for the hotbar, pickup prompt, settings controls, and mobile controls.
- Test gameplay, modal interactions, and save restoration.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer is unsupported without accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage.

## Next Move
1. Implement `openShop()` and purchases; `shopBtn` currently references this undefined function.
2. Add feature-specific CSS for the hotbar, pickup prompt, settings, and mobile controls.
3. Run syntax and browser checks, especially game initialization, shop interactions, and save restoration.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, persistence, settings, crafting, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game UI, hotbar/shop entry point, and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Existing styling; feature-specific additions remain.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` has two `showCatchModal` declarations; the later declaration overrides the earlier one.
- `openSettings()` already binds persistent controls, including settings and HUD visibility.
- This turn inspected existing files but made no changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete gameplay systems in the existing AQUARIA game while preserving its world, visual style, and working features.
- Keep gameplay persistent and mobile-friendly; clarify that multiplayer is unsupported without a real backend.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Make features gameplay-connected, persistent, and mobile-friendly.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview; real multiplayer requires backend infrastructure and is not simulated.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added hotbar, pickup prompt, shop entry point, touch controls, item metadata, and local persistence for gameplay state and settings.
- Improved movement collision, water detection, safe-position recovery, respawn, fishing bait use, mobile action handlers, crafting, and dropped-item behavior.
- Implemented shop purchases for bait, blocks, coral, golden rod, and hooks with coin/ownership checks and local save updates.
- Added responsive styling for hotbar, pickup prompt, settings, shop, and touch controls.
- Verified `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and Chromium initialization of the UI/hotbar.

### Active
- Further test gameplay interactions, shop and modal behavior, mobile layouts, and save restoration.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer is unsupported without accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage.

## Next Move
1. Test shop purchases, modal interactions, and save restoration in-browser.
2. Check mobile layout and gameplay controls at narrow viewport sizes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay logic, persistence, settings, crafting, interactions, and shop.
- `index.html`: Game UI, hotbar/shop entry point, and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` has duplicate `showCatchModal` declarations; the later declaration overrides the earlier one.
- `shopBtn` is wired to `openShop()`.
- Local preview was started at `http://127.0.0.1:4173`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete gameplay systems in the existing AQUARIA game while preserving its world and working features.
- Make the game fully landscape and turn the hotbar into a slide-up inventory with a 15-item starting limit, upgradeable to 300 using gems.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Keep gameplay persistent and mobile-friendly.
- Real multiplayer is unsupported without a backend; do not simulate it.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.
- Inventory capacity starts at 15 and is upgradeable to a maximum of 300 with gems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added hotbar, pickup prompt, shop entry point, touch controls, item metadata, and local persistence for gameplay state and settings.
- Improved movement collision, water detection, safe-position recovery, respawn, fishing bait use, mobile action handlers, crafting, dropped-item behavior, and shop purchases.
- Added responsive styling for existing gameplay UI and controls.
- Began capacity-system work: `game.js` state now initializes `gems` to 5 and `inventoryLimit` to 15.

### Active
- Finish the landscape layout and slide-up inventory UI.
- Persist gems and inventory capacity; implement capacity upgrades capped at 300.
- Enforce capacity when collecting items and catching fish.
- Test shop/modal interactions, save restoration, and narrow/mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer requires accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage.

## Next Move
1. Add `gems` and `inventoryLimit` to save data and display them in the UI.
2. Implement the expandable inventory panel, upgrade purchase flow, and capacity checks.
3. Adjust layout for landscape/mobile use and verify behavior and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay state, persistence, inventory, controls, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game UI, hotbar, toolbar, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Main and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` has duplicate `showCatchModal` declarations; the later declaration overrides the earlier one.
- `shopBtn` is wired to `openShop()`.
- Before the latest request, `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and Chromium UI/hotbar initialization were verified.
- Gems/capacity state initialization has been changed, but persistence and gameplay/UI integration are not complete.

## Objective
- Complete gameplay systems in the existing AQUARIA game while preserving its world and working features.
- Keep gameplay landscape-oriented and make the hotbar a slide-up inventory with a 15-item starting limit, upgradeable to 300 using gems.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Keep gameplay persistent and mobile-friendly.
- Real multiplayer is unsupported without a backend; do not simulate it.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.
- Inventory capacity starts at 15 and is upgradeable to a maximum of 300 with gems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added gameplay UI, hotbar, pickup prompt, shop entry point, touch controls, item metadata, local persistence, and improvements to movement, fishing, crafting, dropped items, and shop interactions.
- Persisted gems and inventory capacity; added a gem wallet, inventory capacity display, and gem-based backpack upgrades.
- Enforced capacity on item pickups and fish catches.
- Added slide-up modal styling and landscape/mobile layout adjustments.

## Objective
- Complete gameplay systems in the existing AQUARIA game while preserving its world and working features.
- Keep gameplay landscape-oriented, with mobile touch controls and a slide-up inventory starting at 15 slots and upgradeable to 300 using gems.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Keep gameplay persistent and mobile-friendly.
- Real multiplayer is unsupported without a backend; do not simulate it.
- Show movement and jump controls in landscape; use a free analog movement pad on the left and jump on the right.
- Add an “Edit HUD” controller option in Settings.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.
- Inventory capacity starts at 15 and is upgradeable to a maximum of 300 with gems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added gameplay UI, hotbar, pickup prompt, shop entry point, touch controls, item metadata, local persistence, and improvements to movement, fishing, crafting, dropped items, and shop interactions.
- Persisted gems and inventory capacity; added a gem wallet, inventory capacity display, and gem-based backpack upgrades.
- Enforced capacity on item pickups and fish catches.
- Added slide-up modal styling and landscape/mobile layout adjustments.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Fix touch controls: replace left/right buttons with free analog movement; keep controls visible in landscape; place jump on the right.
- Add an “Edit HUD” controller option in Settings.
- Verify inventory/shop interactions, save restoration, and narrow/mobile layouts in a browser.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer requires accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage.

## Next Move
1. Update `index.html`, `game.js`, and `style.css` to implement the requested analog movement pad, right-side jump button, landscape control visibility, and Settings HUD edit toggle.
2. Test landscape and narrow/mobile layouts, bag upgrades, full-inventory behavior, and save restoration at `http://localhost:4173`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay state, persistence, inventory, touch input, Settings, and HUD behavior.
- `index.html`: Game UI and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Main, modal, landscape, and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Gem upgrades cost 3–15 gems per 15-slot increase; initial balance is 5 gems.
- Capacity limits `state.inventory` items, not building-material counts or bait.
- Existing touch controls use `data-move="left"`/`"right"` and `touchLeft`/`touchRight`; movement logic is in `movePlayer()`, jump handling in `jump()`.
- `state.hud` currently supports hotbar, location, and coordinates visibility; Settings is built in `openSettings()`, and styling is applied by `applySettings()`.
- A local preview server was started for port 4173; whether it remains active is unconfirmed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete gameplay systems in the existing AQUARIA game while preserving its world and working features.
- Keep gameplay persistent and mobile-friendly, with landscape touch controls and a slide-up inventory.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing world, terrain, water, environment, progress, and working features; do not rebuild or replace the project.
- Keep gameplay persistent and mobile-friendly.
- Real multiplayer is unsupported without a backend; do not simulate it.
- Show movement and jump controls in landscape; use a free analog movement pad on the left and jump on the right.
- Add an “Edit HUD” controller option in Settings.

## Decisions
- The game remains a single-player local preview.
- Existing saves continue using `aquaria-stage1-v1`.
- Inventory capacity starts at 15 and is upgradeable to a maximum of 300 with gems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added gameplay UI, hotbar, pickup prompt, shop entry point, touch controls, item metadata, local persistence, and improvements to movement, fishing, crafting, dropped items, and shop interactions.
- Persisted gems and inventory capacity; added a gem wallet, inventory capacity display, and gem-based backpack upgrades.
- Enforced capacity on item pickups and fish catches.
- Replaced left/right touch buttons and the extra mobile action cluster with an analog pad and right-side jump button in `index.html`; added analog pointer input handling and persisted HUD edit state in `game.js`.

### Active
- Finish the Settings “Edit HUD” toggle and its save/apply behavior.
- Add analog pad, jump button, and HUD editing visual styles; ensure controls remain visible in landscape.
- Verify inventory/shop interactions, save restoration, and narrow/mobile layouts in a browser.

### Blocked
- Real multiplayer requires accounts, an authoritative server, and persistent multiplayer storage.

## Next Move
1. Add the Settings “Edit HUD” option and its event handling in `game.js`, then ensure toggling saves and applies state.
2. Add responsive styling for the analog pad, jump control, and HUD edit mode in `style.css`.
3. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`, then test landscape/mobile layouts and gameplay at `http://localhost:4173`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay state, persistence, inventory, touch input, Settings, and HUD behavior.
- `index.html`: Game UI and analog/jump touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Main, modal, landscape, and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Gem upgrades cost 3–15 gems per 15-slot increase; initial balance is 5 gems.
- Capacity limits `state.inventory` items, not building-material counts or bait.
- Analog control now sets `keys.touchLeft`, `keys.touchRight`, and `keys.touchJump`; `movePlayer()` consumes these flags.
- HUD visibility supports hotbar, location, and coordinates; `applySettings()` now toggles `.hud-editing` from `state.hud.edit`.
- The `openSettings()` markup and handlers have not yet been updated with an Edit HUD option.
- Analog pad markup uses `#analogPad` and `#analogStick`; jump remains `#mobileJump`.
